answer: A registry scores agents by stake-weighted attestations from distinct, rate-limited issuers and clusters wallets by shared funding provenance; each cluster’s reward follows a concave curve, so splitting stake across many keys does not increase total payout. Fake identities must lock real capital, pay issuance fees, and risk graph-link exposure, while a spiral of re-funding and opal-patterned attestation rings is flagged; a mirror check compares funding and behavior graphs. Limitation: slow colluders can mimic independence, and privacy-preserving funding hides provenance.
